title: Set up your dev tools
canDo: install VS Code, Node, and use browser DevTools

blocks.md: Every developer needs three things before writing a single line of code: a place to write it (a code editor), a way to run it (Node.js), and a way to inspect it in the browser (DevTools). This session is pure setup — by the end your machine will be ready and you will have confirmed each tool is working.
By the end of this session you will be able to install and verify VS Code, Node.js (current LTS), and open browser DevTools.
blocks.canDo: install VS Code, Node, and use browser DevTools

blocks.md: **VS Code** is a free code editor made by Microsoft — it highlights syntax, suggests completions, and integrates with Git. **Node.js** lets JavaScript run outside the browser; it also ships **npm** (Node Package Manager), which you will use to install libraries throughout this course. The current LTS in 2026 is **v24** — after installing, run `node --version` in a terminal and confirm it prints `v24.x.x`. **Browser DevTools** (open with F12 or right-click → Inspect) has two tabs you will use constantly: **Console** (runs JS, shows errors) and **Elements** (inspect and live-edit the page HTML/CSS). No code to write yet — follow the steps, verify each tool, move on.

### The Odin Project — Installations

The Odin Project's Foundations path walks you through the full installation for your OS (macOS, Linux, or Windows/WSL). Complete every step in that section, then come back here for the quiz.

**What to do:** open the link, pick your operating system, follow every installation step, then return.
blocks.label: Foundations — Installations (OS-specific)

blocks.md:
**Quick verification checklist** — run these three commands in your terminal after the installs:

```
node --version   # should print v24.x.x
npm --version    # should print 11.x.x or higher
code --version   # should print a VS Code version number
```

If `code --version` errors on macOS, open VS Code, press **Cmd+Shift+P**, type `shell command`, and select **Install 'code' command in PATH**.

questions.question: When you install Node.js, what else gets installed automatically that you will use to add libraries to your projects?
questions.explanation: Node.js ships with npm, the package manager you use to install JavaScript libraries and tools.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of browser DevTools (F12)?
options: To write and save HTML files to your hard drive
To inspect, debug, and live-edit a web page's code and console output
To upload files to a web server
questions.explanation: DevTools lets you inspect HTML/CSS in the Elements panel and run or debug JavaScript in the Console panel.

questions.question: Which Node.js version should you install in 2026 to get the current Long-Term Support (LTS) release?
questions.explanation: The current LTS in 2026 is Node v24. After installing, `node --version` should print v24.x.x.

blocks.md:
Your machine now has VS Code, Node.js v24, and browser DevTools ready to go. That is the full foundation every project in this course will build on.

**Next up:** version control with Git — so you never lose work and can share your code with the world.
